article_title: Strengthening patient safety competencies among physician interns through a structured quality and safety course.
citation: Qureshi Muhammad Fazal Hussain; Asif Fozia; Khan Shahmeer Raza; Akhtar Munazza; Shah Muzna; Altaf Ahmed; Latif Asad. (2026). Strengthening patient safety competencies among physician interns through a structured quality and safety course. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-09875-4
title: Structured Quality and Patient Safety (QPS) module for postgraduate medical interns
description: A compulsory module in the internship curriculum at a private tertiary care hospital in Pakistan, consisting of "a pre-module online assessment administered through the institutional Virtual Learning Environment, followed by two consecutive in-person teaching days (13 contact hours)". Morning didactic lectures cover quality and patient safety, the science of safety, error disclosure, safety culture, and conflict management, followed by facilitated group-based applied learning including case-based learning on learning from defects, a communication lab, and structured case-based discussions, concluding with a post-module assessment.
requirements: Delivered as a compulsory component of the internship curriculum with pre- and post-module assessments administered through the institutional Virtual Learning Environment
constraints: The one-arm quasi-experimental design precluded a concurrent control group and limits causal attribution of observed gains
target_learners: Postgraduate medical interns in a one-year internship programme at a tertiary care hospital
target_learning_goals: Knowledge efficacy for safety and quality improvement practices
examples: Two consecutive in-person teaching days with 13 contact hours combining didactic lectures and applied learning activities such as case-based learning exercises and a communication lab
